practiceReport.name: Jacob Rodriguez
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Every-down starter workload (99% snaps) — 82% active conversion baseline when logging Limited Friday reps.
practiceReport.beatComment: With Miami trailing 20-3 in the second quarter, Rodriguez picked off Josh Allen and returned it to Buffalo's 22-yard line to help set up a Dolphins field goal. It was the second-round rookie linebacker's second interception of the season, and his 13 tackles were his third-highest total in a single game. He's up to 93 tackles (44 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two interceptions and a forced fumble while playing 99 percent of the Dolphins' defensive snaps.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Ronnie Harrison Jr.
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Harrison suffered a hamstring injury in Week 1 that landed him on injured reserve. The fact the Dolphins opted to open his practice window after nine weeks suggests Harrison may be nearing a return.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Malik Willis
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: That said, per Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com, Hafley added that the Dolphins will evaluate the QB's status again depending on how he feels at the end of his minimum required stay on IR. For now, Willis is out for at least three more games, with Kyle McCord currently filling in as 1-9 Miami's starting signal-caller.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Cole Turner
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: The tight end was waived/injured by Miami on Wednesday. Now that he has cleared waivers and moved to IR, Turner will need to reach an injury settlement with the Dolphins to have a chance to play in 2026. The former Titan and Commander has 13 catches for 143 yards and no touchdowns across three NFL seasons.

irAndReserveTracker.name: De'Von Achane
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Achane's move to injured reserve was merely a formality after head coach Jeff Hafley confirmed earlier Monday that the running back would be lost for the season after sustaining an ACL tear in his left knee during Sunday's 24-10 loss to Kansas City. With Achane out of the mix for the rest of 2026, the Dolphins are left with Jaylen Wright (foot) and Ollie Gordon as the lone running backs on the 53-man roster.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Jordan Phillips
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Phillips was recently placed on injured reserve with a season-ending biceps injury sustained in Week 10 versus the Colts. The 22-year-old ends his season with 28 tackles (11 solo) through nine games. Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper are top candidates to see more reps at defensive tackle as the season continues.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Rene Konga
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Placed on Injured Reserve (Undisclosed) on Aug 5, 2026; ineligible to return in 2026 under NFL CBA rules.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Zach Sieler
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: This move was anticipated after Sieler suffered a ruptured biceps in Sunday's Week 9 loss to the Lions. The veteran defensive tackle is scheduled for surgery and will finish his ninth NFL campaign with 24 tackles, including 2.0 sacks. Zeek Biggers, Kenneth Grant and Jordan Phillips could all take on more defensive snaps with Sieler sidelined for the rest of the season.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Zeek Biggers
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Biggers suffered a lateral meniscus tear in Week 10, and he will now miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign while on IR. Fellow defensive lineman Jordan Phillips (biceps) was also placed on IR on Tuesday, and as a result, Kenneth Grant will operate as the team's top dog at defensive tackle moving forward this season.
